title: Lesson 23: Error Handling and Monitoring: Debug Logs, Event Monitoring, Health Checks, and Alerts
description: The observability layer of a Salesforce org: debug logs and trace flags when a transaction misbehaves, Event Monitoring when you need who, what, and when across the whole org, health checks for the security baseline and the platform status, and the alerting that turns all of it into action instead of archaeology.

questions.question: Heavy logging on a frequently accessed Apex class can cause which problem in production?
options: It permanently deletes older captured logs
It disables the org's daily API allocation
The logging itself can make the requests fail
It prevents new trace flags from being created
questions.explanation: A trace flag on a hot class or busy user adds overhead, so production debugging is done surgically with a short-lived flag on the specific path.

questions.question: Which question does Event Monitoring answer that a single debug log cannot?
options: Why one specific callout failed inside a single failing transaction
Whether a validation rule rejected a particular record
Which line of Apex threw an exception during a request
Who accessed what data, when, and from where across the org
questions.explanation: A debug log explains one transaction, while Event Monitoring provides organization-wide performance, security, and usage data to attribute activity.

questions.question: An org's API calls are rejected with a limit-exceeded error even though the daily limit is described as soft. What explains this?
options: Pushing past the soft limit trips a protection block until usage falls back
The soft limit was removed in a recent platform release
Only Bulk API calls actually count against the daily limit
The org's license tier blocks all API calls after the daily reset at midnight
questions.explanation: The daily limit allows overage, but pushing far enough trips a system protection wall that returns an error until 24-hour usage drops below the limit.
